sentences.text: Xixianykus is classified as an alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur, a group of small, specialized predators.
The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
Xixianykus was a small animal approximately 50 cm long, 20 cm high, and weighing about 0.74 kg.
Xixianykus likely had feathers, small robust arms with large claws, and a tubular snout adapted for feeding on colonial insects.
Xixianykus is considered one of the smallest-known non-avian dinosaurs.
Osteohistological analyses confirm that the Xixianykus remains belong to an adult individual, refuting claims that it was a juvenile.
The holotype fossil, designated XMDFEC V0011, was discovered in the Majiacun Formation in Henan Province, China.
The species Xixianykus zhangi was described in 2010 by Xu Xing.
The species name zhangi honors Zhang Xinglao.
Xixianykus exhibits many anatomical adaptations suggesting a cursorial, or running, lifestyle.
Xixianykus had short femurs combined with long tibias and metatarsi, along with an arctometatarsalian foot structure, indicating it was a fast runner.
Xixianykus is one of the oldest derived alvarezsauroids, belonging to the subfamily Parvicursorinae.
Fossils of Xixianykus were found in the Late Cretaceous (Coniacian-Santonian) Majiacun Formation in Henan, China.
Xixianykus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 87 to 85 million years ago, in the Coniacian and Santonian stages.
The time range for Xixianykus is estimated from 89.8 to 83.6 million years ago.
